name: King of Hena
overview: The King of Hena was a male monarch known primarily for having been defeated by the Assyrian empire, as recorded in 2 Kings 19:13. There is no information about his tribe or other personal details. His role in Scripture is limited to this mention of his defeat.
namesAndTitles: This figure is referred to simply as the 'King of Hena,' a title that directly identifies him as the ruler of the region called Hena. The name carries no additional meaning beyond this designation and was not given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Hena beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as a defeated king. No relatives or connections are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Hena is significant in the biblical narrative as one of the rulers subdued by Assyria, illustrating the extent of Assyrian dominance during this period. His defeat serves to highlight the geopolitical challenges faced by the nations surrounding Israel and Judah. Although brief, his mention underscores the broader context of Assyrian aggression and the fulfillment of God's sovereign purposes in history.
